blocks.value: A share represents a small piece of ownership in a company. When you buy a share, you become one of the company's owners.

Imagine This: A pizza is cut into eight equal slices. If you own one slice, you own one-eighth of the pizza. Companies work in a similar way—they divide ownership into millions of small pieces called shares.
Instead of selling the entire company to one person, a company divides itself into many shares. Investors buy these shares and become part owners.
If a company has 1,000 shares and you own 10 of them, you own 1% of that company.
Think of a large apartment building with 100 flats. Owning one flat doesn't mean you own the whole building—you simply own one small part. Buying shares works in exactly the same way.
This simple idea of shared ownership is the foundation of the entire stock market.
